content.text:
The drawing is a benzene ring with four substituents, read around the ring as follows:

- The top-right carbon carries NH2.
- The bottom-right carbon carries NO2, so it is adjacent to the NH2 carbon.
- The bottom-left carbon carries CF3.
- The top-left carbon carries Cl.
- The top and bottom vertices of the ring are unsubstituted CH.

Numbering from the NH2 carbon as C1 gives NO2 at C2, an unsubstituted CH at C3, CF3 at C4, Cl at C5, and an unsubstituted CH at C6. The molecule is 5-chloro-2-nitro-4-(trifluoromethyl)aniline.

As SMILES, starting from the NH2 carbon: Nc1cc(Cl)c(C(F)(F)F)cc1[N+](=O)[O-]. Tracing the ring atoms in order:

- c1 is the NH2 carbon (C1).
- c is C6, a CH.
- c(Cl) is C5.
- c(C(F)(F)F) is C4.
- c is C3, a CH.
- c1[N+](=O)[O-] is C2, which closes the ring back to C1.

This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Nc1cc(Cl)c(C(F)(F)F)cc1[N+](=O)[O-]
